steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Standard conditions: 100 kPa, 298 K, 1 mol dm⁻^3; DeltaH_f deg elements = 0

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hess: DeltaH_total = ΣDeltaH_steps (path independent); Cycle: formation = atomisation + ionisation + electron affinity + lattice

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Born-Haber: DeltaH_f deg = DeltaH_atom + ΣIE + ΣEA + DeltaH_lattice (for ionic compounds)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Bond enthalpies: DeltaH = Σ(bonds broken) - Σ(bonds formed); mean values, gaseous only

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Use Born-Haber cycle to calculate lattice enthalpy of NaCl given: DeltaH_f deg (NaCl) = -411, DeltaH_at(Na)=+107, DeltaH_at(Cl)=+122, IE(Na)=+496, EA(Cl)=-349 kJ/mol --- Solution: DeltaH_f = DeltaH_at(Na) + DeltaH_at(Cl) + IE(Na) + EA(Cl) + LE. -411 = 107 + 122 + 496 - 349 + LE -> LE = -411 - 376 = -787 kJ/mol. Lattice enthalpy = +787 kJ/mol (endothermic to break)

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Define standard enthalpy of combustion | Calculate DeltaH for reaction using bond enthalpies: H₂ + Cl₂ -> 2HCl | Why are mean bond enthalpies less accurate than formation data?

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of energetics with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Use Born-Haber cycle to calculate lattice enthalpy of NaCl given: DeltaH_f deg (NaCl) = -411, DeltaH_at(Na)=+107, DeltaH_at(Cl)=+122, IE(Na)=+496, EA(Cl)=-349 kJ/mol. Solution: DeltaH_f = DeltaH_at(Na) + DeltaH_at(Cl) + IE(Na) + EA(Cl) + LE. -411 = 107 + 122 + 496 - 349 + LE -> LE = -411 - 376 = -787 kJ/mol. Lattice enthalpy = +787 kJ/mol (endothermic to break) Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review
